summary: The verifier checks every README key as an exact typed value, with the lines in sheet order, on sealed hand-checkable sheets. Each CC-2 rule and each figure left to today's code has an isolating case that fails a plausible wrong implementation. It adds relabelled and shuffled hidden sheets, enforces that the driver is byte-identical and imposes no representation the contract does not promise. No confirmed defect was found.
checks_performed: Read tests/expected/10-limits.jsonl in two parts: a Read up to character 44298 (report through L201), then a Grep -o extraction of every L200-L298 and LAST report row plus the shrink field. Together these cover the whole single-line file.

Recomputed by hand every line of the expected reports in families 01-08 (variance, tolerance, status, value, booked) and every sheet's shrink. All match CC-2 rules 2.1-3.4. For lines of other classes, tolerance = today's round(system*5/100), e.g. 250->12 and 350->18 under round-half-even, 30->2. For non-adjusted lines, booked = today's count - system.
Recomputed sheet CC2-0013's shrink (224398083) and CC2-0015's (38230280) in the generated family, plus several of its line tolerances (e.g. B 4241 -> 84, B 490 -> 9, C 2081 -> 104).

Recomputed the limits sheet's shrink by hand from all 61 adjusted-shortage values, including the 100000-unit ABCDEFGHIJKL shortage at cost 1,000,000. The sum is 141219875538 and matches the sealed value. Spot-checked tolerances L18, L147, L151, L179 and LAST.

Traced compare(): exact type-and-value equality on sheet, shrink and every LINE_KEYS field, index by index. Extra keys are ignored. Booked is skipped only for non-adjusted lines outside the families that grade it (test_outputs.py:182-195).
Traced load(): roster digest and row count, rule 1.3 limits on each graded sheet, and other classes confined to families that grade other-class tolerance (test_outputs.py:149-175).

Traced relabel(): fresh unique in-limit SKUs, shuffled lines and a new sheet name, with the expected rows permuted to match and shrink unchanged. This defeats lookups by sheet name, SKU or position (test_outputs.py:250-272).

Traced driver integrity: the delivered bytes are recorded before the verifier copy is installed. test_submitted_driver_unchanged and test.sh's cmp gate the reward (test_outputs.py:57-65, 292-298; test.sh:23-27).

Traced candidate execution: setpriv with no-new-privs as uid 65534, python3 -I -S, an env -i whitelist, a neutral sheet.json path and a fresh cwd. The exit code must be 0 and stdout must parse as JSON (test_outputs.py:104-146).
Mutant reasoning against the sealed fixtures, covering the shipped bugs and other plausible wrong implementations (see coverage_sweep).
Checked that the tests/shipped copy is byte-identical to the environment package (manifest hashes, and read directly). Its report(shipped=True) path is never called, so it cannot affect grading.

coverage_sweep.category: Map each required behavior to an assertion that fails when it is missing or reversed
coverage_sweep.reason: Rule 2.1: 01-recounts R1-R5. Rules 2.3 and 2.4: 02-graded_tolerance, with edge and one-past cases for A, B and C. Rule 3.1: 03-status S1-S6. Rule 3.2: 05 and every family. Rule 3.3: adjusted booked is always compared (R2 count 238 / recount 239 -> -1, not -2). Rule 3.4: 04-shrink. Rule 1.3 limits: 10-limits. Order: index-wise compare plus relabel shuffle.

coverage_sweep.category: Check the full core result (values, membership, required outputs), not just existence or keys
coverage_sweep.reason: Each README key is compared exactly with type identity, including shrink and sheet. Line count and position are asserted, so a partial or constant report fails.

coverage_sweep.category: Named domain rules each have a case whose outcome changes when the rule is wrong
coverage_sweep.reason: Ignoring recounts fails R1, R3 and R4. A falsy-zero recount bug (recount or count) fails R4 and R5. Rounding instead of dropping the fraction fails B3/B4 and C3/C4 (1049*2% = 20.98, 119*5% = 5.95). Using the percentage of the final count instead of system fails B3 (21 vs 20). The shipped status without 'recount' fails S1, S3 and S5. Booked = count - system on adjusted lines fails R2 and R4. The shipped signed -sum shrink gives -2600 on CC2-0006 and fails. Counting surpluses or recount-status shortages fails CC2-0005. Clamping shrink at nought fails CC2-0005 (43300 expected). A missing abs() fails K3.

coverage_sweep.category: Figures left to today's code (other-class tolerance, non-adjusted booked) are graded consistently with the contract
coverage_sweep.reason: instruction.md:3 keeps today's step for figures the procedure does not define. The goldens use round(system*5/100) for classes D-Z and count - system for non-adjusted booked. X1 (12.5 -> 12), X3 (17.5 -> 18) and X7 (1.5 -> 2) reject floor, round-half-up and class-C treatment. N4, N5, N7 and N8 reject booked = variance and booked = 0. These figures are graded only in their own families, and load() keeps other classes out of every other family.

coverage_sweep.category: Signed derived quantities: legal sign partitions discriminated
coverage_sweep.reason: Variance and value cover negative, zero and positive. The tolerance edge is tested on both sides for C (C1 -5 ok / C2 -6 adjust / C3 +5 ok / C4 +6 adjust), for B (B1 +20, B2 +21, C8 -2000 at tolerance 2000) and for A (-1 and +1). Shrink covers zero with only adjusted surpluses (CC2-0006), positive with a mix (CC2-0005, 08) and excluded recount-status shortages. No invariant relies on approximate equality to zero.

coverage_sweep.category: Plausible incorrect solution rejected; hardcoding or proxy rewarded
coverage_sweep.reason: The sheets are hidden and varied. Relabelling with fresh SKUs and names, and shuffling lines, defeats lookups keyed on sheet name, SKU or position. Each sheet runs in a fresh process with a neutral input path.

coverage_sweep.category: Contract-valid alternatives accepted (formatting, ordering, implementation choices)
coverage_sweep.reason: Output is parsed with json.loads, so key order and whitespace are free. Extra keys are ignored. Only integer/string types and line order are enforced, both of which instruction.md:5 promises. The candidate may restructure /app/src freely; only the driver must be byte-identical, as instruction.md:1 states. Every fixture is within rule 1.3, and no fixture uses the open inputs (duplicate SKUs, out-of-limit values).

coverage_sweep.category: Documented restrictions enforced (driver unchanged, report via documented command)
coverage_sweep.reason: The delivered driver's bytes are compared with the shipped copy. The verifier copy is installed and re-checked after all runs, and test.sh cmp gates the reward. The documented command is used for every sheet.

coverage_sweep.category: Stale binaries, self-controlled comparisons, unreachable test cases
coverage_sweep.reason: Expected values are sealed goldens with roster digests; there is no candidate-supplied checksum or comparison. The candidate's source is executed directly (PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE set, /app sealed read-only). Every family is loaded and checked, and the limits test asserts 300 lines. The unused shipped=True path has no grading effect.

coverage_sweep.category: Golden correctness (tests do not enforce wrong behavior)
coverage_sweep.reason: Recomputed all family 01-08 lines and shrinks, two generated-sheet shrinks and the full limits-sheet shrink by hand. All agree with CC-2 and with the contract's today's-code rule.
The report is a stateless per-line mapping plus a sum; there is no event-driven state machine.

coverage_sweep.category: Native encoding / layout / diagnostic-output representation promises
coverage_sweep.reason: The only representation promises are JSON integer or string types and line order (instruction.md:5), and the verifier enforces exactly those. It does not compare stdout bytes, file layout or diagnostics.

coverage_sweep.category: Instruction-promised input classes present in graded sheets
coverage_sweep.reason: Coverage of each promised input class: 1-line (CC2-0008) and 300-line sheets; all class letters (A-C across families, D-Z in CC2-0009); system quantities 0 and 100000; counts and recounts above, below and equal to system; recounts that bring a line back inside tolerance (R3, S4) and ones that do not (S2, S6); variances on the edge and one past; fractional tolerances; and sheets mixing shortages and surpluses.

interaction_sweep.case_or_path: The count is within tolerance but the recount is outside (R4: count 100 = system, recount 0 -> adjust). The count is outside but the recount is back inside (R3, S4 -> ok). This rejects implementations that decide status from the count.
R2 adjusted with count != recount (booked -1). N4, N5, N7 and N8 are ok with count != recount (booked = count - system). T1 in the mixed family is graded too.
EG (class G, no recount, over tolerance) -> recount. EH, X2 and X5 (other class, recount, over) -> adjust. T2 is an adjusted shortage of class N and contributes 19000 to shrink 19800.
K4 is a shortage awaiting recount and is excluded. K2 and K6/K7 are surpluses and do not reduce shrink (CC2-0005 = 43300, CC2-0006 = 0).
System 0 gives tolerance 0 for B, C and other classes (R5, ZZ-9, X5). System 100000 gives B 2000 and C 5000 at the edge (C7 -5001, C8 -2000).
relabel() shuffles lines and reassigns SKUs consistently in the sheet and the expected report. Shrink is unchanged because the line multiset is unchanged.
